response.text:
Endpoint-only supervision already exists in original BERT4Rec: §3.6 explicitly adds training examples masking only the last item, alongside random multi-position reconstruction; inference appends [MASK] and reads its representation. This is not necessarily a separate fine-tuning stage. The authors’ generator creates `dupe_factor` random-mask copies plus one endpoint-only copy per sequence window, then shuffles them together. Thus, merely introducing last-item masking or mixing endpoint and reconstruction examples is not new. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690), [original data generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py).

Normalization matters: paper Eq. 8 averages masked losses within each sequence, whereas the released implementation sums cross-entropies across the minibatch and divides by the total valid target count. Consequently, multi-mask examples receive greater aggregate weight. If endpoint examples comprise fraction p and reconstruction examples average k targets, endpoint-only examples contribute approximately p/[p+(1−p)k] of the target weights—not p. This describes loss coefficients, not guaranteed gradient norms. [Original loss implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py#L353-L366).

Recommended intervention: define each example’s loss as its mean cross-entropy over supervised positions, then use L = α·mean(endpoint-example losses) + (1−α)·mean(reconstruction-example losses), with both groups sampled explicitly. This controls objective coefficients independently of mask count and group size; it cannot guarantee equal gradient magnitudes or directions. If examples instead select endpoint mode with probability p and use an ordinary example mean, p sets the expected mixture weight; applying α again changes that mixture. Specify endpoint sampling, corruption, α, and normalization precisely; evaluate this as explicit reweighting of existing BERT4Rec supervision within one jointly trained model.
